   - High-quality clinical photographs of affected palms and soles.
   - Dermoscopy if available.

3) Diagnostic confirmation / clarification
   - Full pathology report for the punch biopsy (was it taken from an active lesional border? specimen adequacy, orientation, depth). If report truly nondiagnostic, perform a repeat, larger or edge-targeted biopsy (or multiple biopsies) and request evaluation for psoriasiform changes (parakeratosis, regular acanthosis, dilated superficial dermal capillaries, Munro microabscesses).
   - Fungal culture and/or PCR from scrapings to definitively exclude tinea if clinical suspicion remains.
   - If warts suspected, consider HPV-related testing or repeat biopsy evaluated for papillomatosis/koilocytosis.
   - If contact dermatitis suspected, perform patch testing.

4) Therapeutic trial (if diagnosis remains unclear after above)
   - A supervised trial of high-potency topical corticosteroid or a topical keratolytic with close follow-up to assess response can be diagnostic and therapeutic.

Collect and document these data; if they demonstrate classic psoriatic features (clinical pattern, supportive pathology, typical distribution or treatment response) then PASS the diagnosis of palmoplantar psoriasis.
